brief: A wet bar of olive-green savon beldi soap, half-melted and glossy, rests on a hammam ledge of hand-cut zellige tile. The ledge runs edge to edge in a tilted overhead view. The tiles form an interlocking eight-point star pattern in emerald, turquoise, cream and manganese brown. Each glazed chip is slightly wobbly and uneven, with pooled colour and pinholes, built from watercolour fills with marker-drawn grout lines. Soap suds, a few curly hairs, and droplets on the glaze are hyperreal. A sheet of standing water mirrors a blurred brass tap. The air is steamy, warm, and sensual.

A red cabbage is sliced exactly through its equator and seen dead-on. Its convoluted leaf layers form a radial tracery like a cathedral rose window, filling a near-circular field against deep black. The purple-violet leaves glow with translucent watercolour in amethyst, magenta, and cool lilac. The pale veins and white ribs read as stone mullions, outlined with thick dark ink like leading. Moisture beads on the cut face, and the knife's faint drag marks are hyperreal. The colour glows as if lit from behind. The composition is strictly symmetrical and solemn.

The view is through condensation-heavy panes of an old iron glasshouse. A cast-iron mullion grid in dark verdigris cuts the image into tall rectangles. Most panes are fogged pearly grey-green, made with soft wet-in-wet watercolour that blurs palms and ferns into hazy shapes. In one pane, a hand-wiped streak reveals a gardener's face in sharp hyperreal focus: pores, a damp curl of hair, steam on the spectacles. Single drips run down the glass and are rendered precisely, each with its own refracted highlight. The light is humid, diffused and milky. The mood is quiet and private, glimpsed rather than posed.

A long corral of nested shopping trolleys stands in a supermarket car park under flat, shadowless overcast. The view is from directly side-on, so the wire baskets stack into a receding lattice that fills the frame. Everything is rendered in cool graphite pencil, with only faint washes of the store's faded red on the plastic handles. Every weld point, scuff and sticker residue is exact. The sky is a blank pale grey and the tarmac is damp and dull, with no drama. The image is deliberately banal and evenly lit, finding hypnotic beauty in repetition and in the absence of any light event.

An empty municipal tennis court in false-colour infrared, painted in hyperreal detail. The sky is nearly black, a dense indigo-violet wash. The surrounding elms erupt in snow-white and faint coral-pink foliage, built leaf by leaf with sparse watercolour and white gouache-like stippling. The green court surface becomes a strange dusty magenta, with crisp painted lines and a sagging net. Every mesh diamond of the chain-link fence is drawn with a hard graphite pen. A single forgotten yellow ball reads as pale lemon. The low horizon puts the court in the bottom third, with uncanny stillness and grain visible in the washes.

A Golden Age storybook plate in wiry sepia pen line with transparent washes of olive, russet and dusty rose. An old leather hobnail boot lies on its side among roots, and a warty hyperreal toad sits in its opening. The toad's skin is painted with near-photographic fidelity: glands, a golden iris with a horizontal pupil, a moist throat pulse. The boot, roots and twisting tree trunk keep a gnarled, spidery illustrator's line full of hidden faces. The paper is warm and foxed, with a decorative ruled border and a margin left for a caption.

A long horizontal strip of laboratory test tubes in a wooden rack, filled with liquids arranged in perfect hue order. The sequence runs from deep violet through cobalt, viridian and lemon to vermilion and maroon, reading like a continuous spectrum. Across this gradient, sharp dark vertical bands interrupt the colour: menisci, sediment, a rubber stopper, the shadow of a rack post. Together they read as absorption lines. The glass is hyperreal, with refracted label text and condensation beads. The liquids are rendered in luminous layered watercolour, and the dark bands are crisp pen and dense ink.

A goat's head built from flat triangular facets like a low-poly game render. Each polygon is a single even watercolour fill in warm cream, fawn, slate and soft shadow violet, bounded by fine pen edges. One region breaks the mesh: the left eye and its surrounding patch are rendered hyperreal. The horizontal golden pupil, wet lashes, a fly on the lid and individual hairs all bleed out from it, gradually subdividing the neighbouring triangles into finer and finer detail. The head floats against a flat teal void with a soft ambient shadow below.

A chestnut horse lowers its head to drink from a long concrete trough beside towering flat walls of hot magenta and marigold yellow. A sheet of water spills over the trough's edge. The walls are dense, even marker fields with a faint spray grain of plaster. The horse is fiercely hyperreal: veins along the neck, a wet muzzle, light catching every hair of the mane. A sharp diagonal shadow slices the composition into geometric blocks against a hard cerulean sky. It is architectural, silent and monumental.

A sleeping newborn's face and curled fist emerge from deep smoky shadow, modelled entirely through sfumato. Soft charcoal mass is blended over warm tinted paper until no edge exists, with sanguine and umber glazes floated in the cheeks. Hyperreal detail lives only in the light: milk spots on the nose, translucent eyelids with fine veins, downy hair on the temple, a wet lower lip. Everything else dissolves into a hazy, misty grey-blue background like a distant Leonardo landscape. The picture is hushed and intimate.

A full achievement of arms in which every charge is painted hyperreal. Two iridescent bronze-and-rust roosters stand rampant as supporters, each feather lit and individually barbed. The shield beneath them is quartered with sliced pomegranates whose arils glisten like garnets. The mantling unfurls as real crumpled crimson silk. Gold areas are built with dense ink hatching in the old tincture codes, and argent is left as bare vellum. The palette is limited to heraldic vermilion, azure, sable and an ochre-gold. Everything is symmetrical, frontal and ceremonially stiff, yet tactile enough to pluck.

An airline safety card laid out as a tidy sequence of rounded panels. Hands pull the toggle on a life vest that swells from a flat pouch to a taut, glossy chrome-yellow bladder. Panels advance left to right through flat, airbrushed watercolour, with clean marker outlines in navy. Each pair of hands and each vest is uncannily real: knuckle creases, a wedding band, nylon webbing, the crinkle and specular gleam of rubberised fabric. Bold red arrows and dashed motion lines are inked crisply. The panels sit on a pale grey-blue card stock with a faint spray of printing grain.

A kirigami pop-up card opened flat, rising from its centre fold into a brownstone stoop with a sleeping beagle sprawled on the top step. Every cut layer is cream card rendered in meticulous graphite: the score lines, slight paper fuzz at the knife edges, and soft cast shadows stepping back plane by plane. The dog alone is coloured, in warm hyperreal pencil showing whisker pores, a twitching ear and tan-and-white fur. Seen from a low three-quarter angle, the whole construction reads as both delicate paper engineering and a living scene.

A button accordion shattered into overlapping translucent facets in the manner of Analytic Cubism. Each shard is rendered with photographic precision: pearl celluloid keys, bellows folds with worn leather corners, nickel grille holes, a frayed shoulder strap. The palette is restricted to raw umber, ochre, slate grey and bone, built up in charcoal mass and graphite hatching. Shards interpenetrate along a loose central pyramid, and shallow-angle hatching scuttles across the gaps. The picture is a scaffold of shifting viewpoints in which every fragment looks touchable.

A Turkish ebru marbling bath seen from directly above. Combed rivers of indigo, carmine, saffron and moss green have been dragged into nonpareil feathers and swirls by a flow of wet watercolour. Resting on the surface, half-sunk, lies a hyperreal antique silver teaspoon. Its bowl mirrors the marbled pattern in compressed, curved distortion, with tarnish in its engraved handle and a bead of water at its tip. Paint flows bend around the spoon with a tiny meniscus halo. The fluid, organic ground is contrasted with the cold, exact metal.

A rectangular cast-bronze relief plaque in Benin court style, showing a contemporary fishmonger rendered with hyperreal intensity. He holds two mudfish by the gills and wears a stacked coral bead collar over a modern football jersey. The background is filled with stamped quatrefoil river-leaf patterns. Figures sit frontal and hierarchic, in high relief, with pen hatching for incised textures. Copper-brown, verdigris and dark patina are built in layered watercolour, with polished highlights where hands would have rubbed. Fish scales, beard stubble and the jersey's weave all register as both cast metal and living flesh.

An overhead view of a crowded domino game read as a figure-ground city plan. The ivory tiles form dense blocks and streets, and the green baize between them is flooded with solid black ink, so the layout reads as Nolli-map poché. Seen closer, each tile is hyperreal: chipped edges, yellowed bone surfaces, drilled pips holding dust, fingerprints of grease. Narrow gaps act as alleys, and a scattered open plaza holds a coffee ring stain and a fallen coin. There is no perspective, only a crisp, cartographic flatness with shadows cut exactly.

A black bear's face split down the middle and unfolded flat in Northwest Coast fashion. It is bounded by swelling black formline ovoids and U-forms, with secondary formlines in vermilion, on a pale cedar-plank ground with visible grain. Inside each formline enclosure, the bear is painted hyperreal: coarse guard hairs, a damp leathery nose, a glinting amber eye, yellowed teeth. The ink edges are razor-crisp and tapered, contrasting against the soft, dense fur rendered with pencil and charcoal. The result is strict symmetry with a pulse.

A dense, saturated dye-transfer colour print of a turquoise 1960s sedan's rear fin and red taillight, parked in an empty supermarket lot at dusk. Deep watercolour is glazed layer upon layer until the colours feel lacquered: turquoise body paint, a cherry-red lens, oxblood shadows, and a sodium-amber sky reflected in the chrome. Bumper reflections are crisp but slightly warped. Asphalt cracks run past an oil stain with a faint rainbow sheen. The framing is off-centre and banal, like a snapshot, but colour density is pushed until ordinary metal feels emotionally heavy.

A Synthetic Cubist papier collé made trompe l'oeil. Cut scraps of yellowed newspaper, faux-bois wallpaper, a striped café menu and blue tissue overlap at angles, each one rendered so convincingly it seems physically pasted. Lifting corners, glue wrinkles and torn fibres are all painted. Over and between the scraps sit a hyperreal half-smoked cigar with a curl of ash, a crumpled matchbook, and a stemmed glass outlined in loose charcoal. Flat planes of ochre, olive and black anchor the arrangement on a buff ground.
